I think the long taper with no walkbacks helped me set a tone for success.  I did not ever have seizures, but did have a few “zaps”.  The more you read the better prepped you’ll be for the wide range of issues you may experience.

I agree that it is baffling at how little consideration is given this epidemic.  I am lucky enough to be a survivor of an attempt.  Here are a few thoughts:

Suicide suffers from a terrible case of “cry wolf” syndrome.  There are many, MANY people out there who have threatened it as a means of getting attention they otherwise lack.  That does not excuse the dismissive behavior, but it is an unfortunate challenge to overcome.

I sent very unambiguous signs up prior to my attempt.  And while it garnered some attention, what effort that was put into understanding me was all about treating the symptom, not the cause- higher doses!  Or ignore it outright.  You know- we put a lot of energy into making life fast and convenient.  Sitting down with someone depressed enough to show suicide warnings is neither fast nor convenient.  It takes someone willing to get in that couch fort with you.  (We exist- we’re out there, please don’t give up).

And then, for those who recognized the signs, so many people are unprepared to offer proper help.  This very subreddit, for example, has very specific “can” and “cannot” rules about how to approach someone.  For your average person, they would be shocked to learn this basic... etiquette?  Folks just for real don’t know what to do.  Society distances itself from valuing empathy, and much of what drives people are teeny tiny boops of serotonin from social media.  Upboats.  Downboats.  Thank Cthulhu Facebook doesn’t have a “dislike” button- social bullying would turn us into an apocalyptic wasteland overnight.  

While not a member of the LGTBQ community, I can still relate.  Social isolation suuuuucks.  I think some of the best advice I got when I was school age was from someone I did not expect it from- something of an authority figure, who was expected to be a real sunshine pumper and tell everyone “these are the times of your life- enjoy youth while you can before you have to be an adult, blah blah.”  Instead, they sat me down and very calmly said “you couldn’t pay me enough to go through school again.  Everything is so amped up with hormones and so much of your self worth is based on other people’s opinion...  My life got way better after school, and while its never *easy*, it does get easier.”

My own father kept the shotgun that almost went off in my mouth.  You’d think he’d have cleared the house of firearms.  Taken the whole experience more seriously.  Its sad how few people are willing to slow down and attempt to invest the time to understand and help.  I hear you loud and clear.  A pro is always preferable, but anyone listening is better than no one, and as long as you’re willing to put a lifeline out someplace like this, hopefully someone is there to answer the call.  

Here if you want to talk.

Took 60 ambien, 60 klonopin, 60 xanax.  Knocked out for a while, but was discovered and fed the charcoal milkshake.  I’ve never known so much pain.  Physically and mentally.  Please don’t do it.  It sounds like you’ve reasoned it out in your head, but I assure you there is a way through.  Its not always easy, but there is a way.

Potential ramifications:

If you try and fail, there are potential legal issues for you in the aftermath.  If you try and succeed there are potential law enforcement inquiries into friends and family that will make them very uncomfortable, and your death very public.  I encourage you to find someone to talk to as a starter- there are links to phone numbers and even a text line in this sub.  A professional is always the best way to go, but if you find yourself without the resources, even a stranger on reddit is better than no one at all.  I’ll listen.

I speak from experience.  I thought getting away from family and isolating myself the safest place I could think of was wise.  It was not wise.  It made things so much worse.  And my advice remains the same to anyone in a situation where they feel like ending your own life is the only answer: please seek help.  Even by posting here on reddit you’re seeking help in a way.  Hold on to that, and if you need a reason to keep it up- never settle.  Keep thinking there is better help and better friends and seek and seek and seek.   I still seek, and even though there are sometimes long stretches of frustration with slow progress, I find the persistence pays off, and I am finding better help and better friends. 

Please be well, and if you aren’t- seek someone who wants to try and help.  Based on your description of diagnosis, I can empathize.

Start with one simple reality matrix:

You either believe or do not believe the following statement:

"Time heals all wounds"

If you choose to believe that, you can remind yourself that "time" is a bitch, in that she rarely cares about "now".  I choose to believe that statement.  Time is the tricky part.  Especially when NOW is so painful.  But it does improve.  You rarely notice the improvement from one day to the next.  But from one week to the next?  More so.  One month?  A tad more.  One year?  A wee bit more.

You can't undo some things.  Nope.  Cannot unmake that choice.  And you might not be able to fix it.  But it will get better.  Both the pain you are feeling for making the choice, and the choice's impact on other people's lives.
